findings_addressed: FIX-2 [P2] 1/3 — CycloneDX validity was SELF-CERTIFIED (test_cyclonedx.py:99-100). AC-SBOM-10 proved schema validity by calling `sbom_survey.cyclonedx.validate()`, a function FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION UNDER TEST, so an implementation whose validate() returned None unconditionally passed while emitting invalid CycloneDX JSON — precisely the hand-rolled-SBOM failure the criterion exists to stop. CLOSED with an INDEPENDENT oracle: `conftest.independent_cyclonedx_validator()` builds `cyclonedx.validation.json.JsonStrictValidator(SchemaVersion.V1_6)` from the UPSTREAM library, which design §5.7 already declared as a dependency (`cyclonedx-python-lib[json-validation]`) for exactly this purpose. A known-invalid NEGATIVE CONTROL runs FIRST — `KNOWN_INVALID_CYCLONEDX_DOC`, whose only component omits the `type` field CycloneDX 1.6 makes required — so an oracle that accepts everything is caught before any clean verdict from it is believed. The tool's own validate() survives only as a cross-check required to AGREE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: None for the real document AND a diagnostic for the invalid one; that second half is what a stub cannot fake. Absent-validator posture stated explicitly in §5.7 and enforced by a new `require_external()` helper: a missing distribution FAILS the criterion naming what to install, and NEVER skips — a skip there is the textbook vacuous green, the suite reporting success while the assertion it exists for silently stopped running.

FIX-2 [P2] 2/3 — fixture exclusion was not exercised AT THE SURVEY BOUNDARY (test_tiering.py:105-109). AC-SBOM-06 proved data-drivenness against `TierMap.classify()` alone, so Slice 32 could make classify() fully data-driven while `run_survey()` hardcoded `path.startswith("dev/release/fixtures/")`, passing BOTH AC-SBOM-05 and AC-SBOM-06 with REQ-5's 'never by a hardcoded special case in code' untested where it counts. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-06 now drives BOTH tier maps through `run_survey(..., tier_map=...)`. With the real map, all 8 fixture manifests must appear in `survey.excluded`; with the SAME map minus ONLY the `dev/release/fixtures/` rule, `run_survey` must raise `UntieredManifestError` NAMING a fixture path. No single hardcoded path check can satisfy both rows, which is the point. `run_survey` gains `tier_map` as an optional injectable seam (None => load the tracked tiers.toml); design §5.2 carries the two-row obligation table and §5.4 replaces its elided signature with the full `run_survey(repo_root, *, published, tier_map=None, now=None)`, stating why the last two exist: a rule and a timestamp that cannot be substituted cannot be PROVED load-bearing.

FIX-2 [P2] 3/3 — determinism was tested only on the PINNED-timestamp path (test_report.py:52-54). Both runs passed an explicit `now`, so an implementation defaulting to wall-clock when `now`/`--now` is omitted still passed, though REQ-13 and §5.8 require ORDINARY repeated runs to be byte-identical. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-22 now runs THREE legs — (1) two in-process runs with an explicit `now`; (2) two in-process runs with NO `now` and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` cleared, so the pure built-in default is what gets exercised; (3) two CLI runs with NO `--now`. Byte-equality alone does NOT settle leg 2, because two back-to-back runs can share a wall-clock second and compare identical by luck, so the default `metadata.timestamp` must additionally be MORE THAN 24 HOURS from the real clock. That assertion names no particular epoch (implementation-independent), has a day-wide window (not flaky), and fails exactly when the stamp is the current time. Leg 3 then asserts the CLI's default stamp EQUALS leg 2's, which is what stops `--now` being defaulted to `datetime.now()` inside argparse and handed to run_survey explicitly — a hole legs 1 and 2 would both sail past. Design §5.8 carries the three-leg table and the reasoning.

FIX-1 [P2] 2/3 (round 1, STILL CLOSED) — no `purl` assertion (test_cyclonedx.py:32-35). REQ-6 requires a purl per component and §5.5 makes the purl the bom-ref — the component identity an advisory feed matches a locked version against — but CycloneDX 1.6 accepts `name` + `version` alone, so a purl-less document passed AC-SBOM-10. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-10 now asserts per component that `purl` is present, carries an ecosystem prefix in {pkg:cargo/, pkg:npm/, pkg:pypi/}, EQUALS the `bom-ref`, and (for resolved components) has an `@version` segment equal to the component's own version; plus a document-level assertion that the purl-type set is EXACTLY {cargo, npm, pypi}. All of it survives fix-2 unchanged; fix-2 only replaced the SCHEMA-VALIDITY oracle in the same test.

FIX-1 [P2] 3/3 (round 1, STILL CLOSED) — dependency-graph coverage was vacuous (test_cyclonedx.py:91-98). `doc.get("dependencies", [])` tolerates an EMPTY array, which is trivially 'closed', and the only depth assertion required a `direct` component — so an implementation emitting the manifest-derived direct set with ZERO lockfile-derived library<->library edges passed, i.e. REQ-8 was unenforced. CLOSED: AC-SBOM-12 asserts the array is non-empty; the graph is closed in BOTH directions (every declared component has a `ref` entry, leaves carrying an empty `dependsOn`); at least one edge originates at a library rather than the metadata root component; and at least one KNOWN LOCKFILE-ONLY crate arrives tagged `transitive`. The sentinel set is proc-macro2 / quote / syn / unicode-ident / serde_derive, each present in the tracked Cargo.lock and declared by NO dependency table of any tracked non-excluded Cargo.toml at cbb56212 — 378 of the 468 locked packages are in that position (the total was misstated as 410 in the fix-1 record and is corrected by the fix-2 sweep above). Only ONE survivor is required, the deliberate drift allowance.
